analyticsOrigin.text: Production `slop.cash` may load Cloudflare Web Analytics through Cloudflare's automatic setup, only to count page views by path and referring site. Cloudflare does not inject into HTML the site's Pages Function serves, so that function adds the same beacon tag on the production host only. The beacon uses no cookies or local storage, logs no query strings and reports to the site's own origin, so private Inbox, case and admin parameters never reach it. Staging, local development and tests never load it. No page depends on it: a blocked or failed beacon changes nothing. Add no other analytics or third-party script without a separate owner decision. The operator proposed this on 11 November 2026; the owner's merge approves it.

provisionalVault.text: The owner may fund a new EVM token vault before it is registered. Once the creation transaction is in a successful canonical block and matches the reviewed request, show the owner the funding form for that vault and state that the creation is not final. Register the vault only from a finalized creation. Count a deposit only from a finalized block and the vault's own deposit event, and only for a registered vault. If the block is replaced, withdraw the form and say so. A deposit confirmed while the vault was not on chain moved nothing; report it as failed, never as received or funded. Native-coin vaults, bounty vaults, other depositors, withdrawals, and Solana vaults wait for registration. Proposed by the operator on 14 November 2026; approved by the owner's merge.

customReferralCode.text: A signed-in member may choose a name for their own referral link (migration `0124_referral_codes.sql`, `backend/referrals/codes.ts`). `/referral/<name>` forwards to the project form with that member's GitHub login as the referrer. The name is only a pointer to the GitHub account: capture, the immutable record and accrual are unchanged. Refuse reserved names, another GitHub account's login, a name another account holds or has held, and administrator and moderator accounts. A member has one name in use, may replace it, and may hold five names in all; a replaced name stops forwarding and stays with its account. A name nobody has in use forwards to the form without a referrer. Settings shows the link and states no reward. The operator proposed this on 14 November 2026; the owner's merge approves it.

solanaScanGenesis.summary: Each Solana scan and vault snapshot read independently checks the configured genesis trust root before reading or changing state.

buybackFinalizedRpc.summary: The private live recovery summary may report an exact finalized read on the configured Robinhood RPC. The diagnostic cannot change accounting or signing.

manualBrowserSmoke.text: Normal releases sync the current D1 registry and collect live GitHub data. An explicit manual main or development release may set `use_published_data` to retain the validated rankings and profiles last published by its own environment (production or staging; operator decision, 13 November 2026). Preserve their timestamps, history, and counts. The option defaults to false and cannot run with bootstrap data. It cannot use the PR adapter or skip any code, browser, sandbox, environment, source, or deployed-byte check. Missing or invalid data stops release. A manual release may separately set `skip_proofs` (section 12, STATE-05); that option leaves out only the state-model and LemmaScript proof stages. Operator decision, 14 November 2026: a manual main or development release may also set `skip_browser_tests`. That run runs the browser smoke lane against the built bundle instead of the complete browser lanes. Pull requests still run the lanes their files affect, and a push release still runs all of them. Bundle, data, integration, installer, sandbox, environment, source and deployed-byte checks still run. The option defaults to false. A release that skipped the browser lanes is not evidence that they passed.

manualProofOmission.text: - **STATE-05 — Verification evidence.** Pin Quint in the lockfile. Run `bun run formal:check` and `bun run formal:verify`. Record tool versions, source hashes, scenarios, backend, finite bounds, results, and unresolved gaps. Distinguish simulation, exhaustive finite exploration, implementation conformance, and live integration. Operator decision, 12 November 2026: an exhaustive verification that runs its whole time allowance without a result is recorded as "not verified within its time bound", shown as a warning, and does not fail the release gate. A counterexample, crash, broken model, unstable input or failed scenario check still fails it, and every identity, command, tool and view check still applies to the timed-out stage. Operator decision, 14 November 2026: an explicit manual main or development release may set `skip_proofs`. That run repeats neither the Quint state-model stages nor the LemmaScript proofs. Pull requests still run the models and proofs their files affect, a push release still runs all of them, and a scheduled run checks all of them on the default branch every night without blocking a release. Both inventory checks and every code, browser, sandbox, environment, source and deployed-byte check still run in the skipping release. The option defaults to false. A release that skipped the proofs is not evidence that they passed.

publicReferredProjects.text: The submitting maintainer may name a signed-in referrer. Keep the record immutable under migration `0055_project_referrer.sql`. Refuse self, steward, administrator, and moderator referrals at capture. Publish the registered projects that carry a referrer at `GET /api/v1/referrals/projects`: project ID, registry status, registration time, and the referrer's GitHub account, oldest first. Every listed project is already public and the accrual files publish the same referrer, so the list has no session and no write route (operator decision, 14 November 2026).
